conviction_note: Lean slightly negative, at p_up 44 on a 3.5% move, giving -0.42. Two peer read-throughs (Q3 NII misses at Handelsbanken and Nordea, and the capital/model overhang that cost SEB -4.6% and Nordea -8.0%) meet a Swedbank-compiled consensus with the most aggressive q/q NII step of the group (+4.1%). Swedbank already fell 2.6% on Nordea's day and 0.95% today on Handelsbanken's, so part of this is priced. SEB reports 30 minutes earlier the same morning, and the two numbers are scored apart by design: the findings sum to -1.1, the scaled number is smaller because both findings are peer inference, not a Swedbank document.

findings.finding: Both Nordic peers that reported Q3 before Swedbank missed NII consensus: Handelsbanken by 1.2% (10,051m vs 10,178m, citing higher funding costs from rising market rates) and Nordea by 0.8% (EUR 1,799m vs 1,814m). Swedbank's own consensus meanwhile assumes NII up 4.1% q/q (11,739m vs 11,276m), and Swedbank's Q2 already named the same headwinds of Swedish mortgage margins and funding costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Swedbank's report-day moves since 2023-10 (Yahoo closes): -6.94, +0.70, +0.96, -1.29, +4.96, +4.18, +3.58, +0.45, -0.24, -0.32, +0.50, -2.99 (Q2 2026, a cost miss), median |move| about 1.1%. Peers on this Q3 NII line: Handelsbanken -2.9% today on an NII miss with operating profit in line, Nordea -8.0% (NII miss plus buyback pause).
findings.original_quote: Nettoeffekten av marginaler och finansieringskostnader påverkade med -194 mkr. Minskningen förklarades av högre finansieringskostnad under kvartalet till följd av högre marknadsräntor. [Handelsbanken: the net effect of margins and funding costs was -194m SEK, explained by higher funding costs in the quarter from higher market rates.] Swedbank Q2: 'lägre bolånemarginaler i Sverige och högre upplåningskostnader påverkade negativt' [lower Swedish mortgage margins and higher funding costs weighed].
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is dated 15 Oct, before Handelsbanken's 21 Oct report, and it still shows the most aggressive q/q NII step of the three banks. If the market had fully repriced the read-through, Swedbank would have tracked Handelsbanken's -2.9% today. It fell 0.95% and is only -3.2% over five sessions. Offsets that limit the size: Swedbank's Baltic engine (Baltic NII +10% q/q in Q2) gets a full quarter of the June ECB hike to 2.25%, a weaker SEK lifts translated NII, and there is the extra day. These are why consensus sits where it does, so the miss is a hypothesis drawn from peers, not a document.
findings.independence: Nordea's Q3 NII also came in below Bloomberg consensus (1,799 vs 1,814; separate source): https://www.placera.se/telegram/nordea-nordea-vantas-redovisa-1-572-miljoner-euro-i-rorelseresultat-bloomberg-20261013 and https://mfn.se/cis/a/nordea-bank/nordea-resultat-for-tredje-kvartalet-2026-1e30e818

findings.finding: FI has announced that from 31 Dec 2026 it will handle IRB-model deficiencies through Pillar 1 (higher REA) instead of Pillar 2, for 'berörda banker'. Applied to SEB on 14 Oct it cut SEB's buffer by 120bp (20bp from the methodology, 100bp from calibration; stock -4.6%), and Nordea paused buybacks on ECB model concerns (-8.0%). Swedbank, with a 2.6% CET1 buffer against a 2.0% target, has quantified nothing yet, and its Q3 report is the first place it can.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Swedbank precedent on this line. Same-month peers: SEB -4.63% on FI's model decision (2026-10-14), Nordea -8.02% on the buyback pause (2026-10-15). Swedbank moved -0.24% and -2.63% on those two days.
findings.original_quote: FI planerar därför att från och med 31 december 2026 övergå från att använda åtgärder i pelare 2 till att använda åtgärder i pelare 1 som huvudsaklig metod för att hantera brister i interna modeller. Detta kommer medföra att sammansättningen av kapitalkravet för berörda banker blir förändrad, genom att det totala kapitalkravet uttryckt i procent blir lägre medan det totala riskvägda exponeringsbeloppet blir högre. [From 31 Dec 2026 FI will move from Pillar 2 to Pillar 1 measures as the main method for model deficiencies; for affected banks the percentage requirement falls while REA rises.] SEB: 'Metodförändringen minskar kapitalbufferten med 20 baspunkter.'
findings.why_not_priced: Swedbank moved only -0.24% on SEB's decision day, so the market did not carry SEB's 120bp to Swedbank. What it does carry is a vague overhang (part of the -2.63% on Nordea's day). Swedbank's own number is unpublished: the Q2 report mentions only the IRK application, nothing on the methodology change, and FI's memo describes the kronor requirement as 'i stort sett oförändrat'. So the disclosure can land as relief or as a hit, which is why the range is wide and the central value small. ECB found deficiencies in Swedbank's Baltic models in Dec 2025, which tilts the tail negative.
